page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-288-metal is a bare-metal server configured with 288 vCPUs and 2232 GB of DDR5 memory. The system is powered by Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors operating at 4.2 GHz across 144 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The architecture includes a 504 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or onboard GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, achieving a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 313057.86 and a PassMark CPU score of 179028.27. Memory subsystem performance is highly efficient, with read bandwidth reaching 1090.07 GB/sec for large uncached blocks and write bandwidth at 412.54 GB/sec. Database operations are a primary strength, as evidenced by a PassMark database score of 40021.03 and Redis SET operations processing at 423.02 million operations per second.

While multi-threaded and memory-bound tasks perform exceptionally well, single-core metrics are more moderate, with stress-ng single-core performance falling into the average tier. Additionally, LLM text generation for smaller models is relatively weak at 42.98 tokens/sec, though medium and large model inference speeds remain strong. Given its massive memory capacity, high memory bandwidth, and high-density compute capabilities, this server is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, heavy software compilation, and complex multi-threaded enterprise workloads.
